subject.title: fix(cron): completed jobs stay stuck behind slower batch runs

question: Should the protected cron scheduling and persistent-state change be approved after branch-specific runtime proof confirms early finalization under a blocked sibling run?
rationale: The `maintainer` label reserves this compatibility-sensitive scheduler and persistent-state behavior for explicit human judgment; automated review cannot substitute for that approval.

options.title: Request runtime proof, then review
options.body: Ask for redacted live or terminal output showing an early completed job clears durable running state while another batch member is still active, then perform the final human review.

options.title: Adopt the prior proof rationale
options.body: If maintainers judge the earlier live proof and the new regression coverage equivalent to this refactor, proceed with normal human review while accepting that proof scope.

recommendation.title: Request runtime proof, then review
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted live or terminal output showing an early completed job clears durable running state while another batch member is still active, then perform the final human review.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier implementation and live proof cover the same terminal-persistence invariant that this PR reworks for the current scheduler architecture.
